title: Universal Declaration, Article 21: participation in government and genuine elections
summary: The United Nations text of Article 21, from the declaration proclaimed on 10 December 1948.
body: The United Nations page of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights gives Article 21. In short: Everyone has the right to take part in the government of their country, directly or through freely chosen representatives, and the right of equal access to public service. The will of the people shall be the basis of the authority of government, expressed in periodic and genuine elections by universal and equal suffrage and by secret vote or by equivalent free voting procedures. The core pack records the proclamation and Article 1. This card is Article 21. The declaration is what the General Assembly proclaimed as a common standard. The UN page opened here does not describe it as a treaty that states ratify.
